title: Every formal algebraic space carries a structure sheaf of topological rings
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that every formal algebraic space has a structure sheaf (statement lines 7664-7667). The proof has four distinct parts. First it reduces the problem to constructing the structure sheaf as a sheaf of topological rings on the small etale site of the space, using the identification of that topos with the site of affine formal algebraic spaces etale over it (proof lines 7669-7674). Second it sets up the category of affine formal algebraic spaces etale and representable over the space, observes that reduction is an equivalence from that category to the small etale site, so that the structure sheaf exists as a presheaf and only the sheaf condition remains (proof lines 7672-7680). Third it analyses a covering: a covering corresponds to a finite family whose reductions form an etale covering, and each member is representable hence affine, and etale by permanence, so that after writing the base as a filtered colimit of its defining affine schemes one obtains an exact sequence for each index, and taking the filtered colimit of these exact sequences -- which is legitimate because limits commute with limits -- produces an exact sequence computing the sections of the structure sheaf (proof lines 7682-7727). Fourth, and separately, it must be checked that the topology on the sections is the one induced from the product, which is done by comparing the fundamental systems of open submodules on the two sides (proof lines 7728-7748). The claim is H3: the category-theoretic reduction, the finiteness and affineness analysis of a covering, the limit of exact sequences, and the compatibility of the limit topology are independent pieces of work, and the last of them is a genuine subtlety about topological rings rather than a formality.
